reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly supports the core premises: it demonstrates that vibrational entropy can be accurately obtained from the covariance matrix of atomic displacements in elemental Na and Al, that a Gaussian approximation (with covariance corrections) works well, and that effective frequencies from the covariance matrix incorporate anharmonicity. The evidence also states that only configurational sampling is needed, not long time evolution, supporting the short-simulation premise. The representation of the evidence is accurate.
premises: Vibrational entropy can be extracted from the covariance matrix of atomic displacements from short AIMD simulations.
A Gaussian approximation for atomic displacements captures essential entropy contributions.
The covariance-based method yields good agreement with experimental entropy for elemental Na and Al.
Effective vibrational frequencies from the covariance matrix incorporate anharmonicity.
The method requires only short, statistically converged simulations, not long trajectories.
